{{Quote|Mandalore's police and emergency services are part of the Mandalorian Guard and attract ''Mando'ade'' who want to protect their people.|[[Tor Vizsla]]|<ref name="TBHC" />}}
The '''Mandalorian Guard''' was an organization that encompassed the combined [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|law enforcement]] and public safety services of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]]. Also known as the '''Mandalorian police''', the [[Officer/Legends|officers]] of the Mandalorian Guard were responsible for upholding law and order, maintaining public welfare, and protecting the various inhabitants of [[Mandalore sector/Legends|Mandalorian Space]]. Within [[New Mandalorians/Legends|New Mandalorian]] territory, the Mandalorian Guard answered to the pacifist [[Ruling Council (New Mandalorians)/Legends|government's]] [[Prime Minister/Legends|Prime Minister]], dispatching organized patrols of [[Color/Legends|grey]]-[[Armor/Legends|armored]] officers to provide the people a sense of order and security, while locally based [[Constable/Legends|constables]] served to enforce the law elsewhere on Mandalore.

==Description==
{{Quote|The Mandalorian Guard includes law enforcement and public-safety units.|Tor Vizsla|<ref name="TBHC" />}}
[[File:MandoSecretService-SWE.png|thumb|left|175px|Officers of the Mandalorian Guard]]
The [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] Guard was an agency that oversaw the combined duties of [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|law enforcement]], public safety, and emergency services for the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]],<ref name="TBHC" /> the Mandalorians' cultural [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] located in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> Highly trained and well organized, the Guard<ref name="TBHC" /> was an elite police force<ref name="GaW">''[[Galaxy at War]]''</ref> whose members were drawn from a multitude of clans, united by a shared desire to protect the Mandalorian people. The [[New Mandalorians/Legends|New Mandalorian]] [[Ruling Council (New Mandalorians)/Legends|government]] monitored the Guard for potential threats to their society, even as a portion of the Mandalorian Guard served the pacifist sect and conducted themselves in accordance to their peaceful ideals.<ref name="TBHC" /> The Guard's New Mandalorian police units answered to the office of the New Mandalorian [[Prime Minister/Legends|Prime Minister]].<ref name="GuardEncyclopedia">{{SWE|groups|mandalorianguard|Mandalorian Guard}}</ref>

Ranks that saw use in the Mandalorian Guard included [[Sergeant/Legends|sergeant]], [[Captain/Legends|captain]],<ref name="Corruption" /> and [[Constable/Legends|constable]].<ref name="I80:HotM">{{InsiderCite|80|The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors}}</ref> Guardsmen were traditionally trained in the use of [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]], [[Flamethrower/Legends|flamethrowers]], and other heavy weapons; those who served within the pacifistic society of the New Mandalorians preferred to make use of [[Stun baton/Legends|stun batons]] and shields as their primary tools, falling back upon more lethal weaponry only as a last resort. Members of the Guard were also trained to be able to work together as a unit,<ref name="TBHC" /> and were capable of [[Pilot/Legends|piloting]] vehicles such as [[Speeder/Legends|speeders]]<ref name="Corruption" /> and [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttles]].<ref name="TCW:DoM">{{TCW|Duchess of Mandalore}}</ref> Among the Mandalorian Guard's elite units were the [[Mandalorian secret service/Legends|Mandalorian Secret Service]]<ref name="TBHC" />—who served the New Mandalorian Prime Minister<ref name="The Academy" /> and received additional training with [[Jetpack/Legends|jetpacks]]—as well as the [[Mandalorian Royal Guard/Legends|Mandalorian Royal Guard]], a detachment charged with protecting the [[Anti-Mandalore|leader]] of the New Mandalorians and their council of [[Minister/Legends|ministers]]. The [[Mandalorian Patrol]] was a division of the Guard that acted as a [[Planetary Security Forces|Planetary Security Force]] for both Mandalore and the [[Mandalore sector/Legends|surrounding sector]] of [[Realspace/Legends|space]], intercepting suspicious vessels with potentially deadly force.<ref name="TBHC" />

==Equipment==
{{Quote|Most Guardsmen wear body armor and use stun batons and shields.|Tor Vizsla|<ref name="TBHC" />}}
Mandalorian Guardsmen typically wore suits of [[Mandalorian armor/Legends|Mandalorian armor]] in the course of their duties.<ref name="TBHC" /> Due to the New Mandalorians' desire to distance their society from that of the Mandalorian warrior clans,<ref name="NewBattlefronts">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: New Battlefronts: The Visual Guide]]''</ref> members of the Guard operating in their territory deviated from contemporary norms as they were more lightly armored, and their plates were of a unique configuration, all [[Color/Legends|colored]] in a uniform grey. New Mandalorian police helmets also forwent the traditional full-faced design baring a T-shaped visor, for one that left the wearer's [[Mouth/Legends|mouth]] exposed,<ref name="TBHC" /> and featured an articulated face guard over the [[Eye/Legends|eyes]] and [[Nose/Legends|nose]] that could be raised and lowered with the touch of a button.<ref name="TCW:DoM" /> Mandalorian constables in other parts of Mandalore<ref name="I80:HotM" /> wore the standard Mandalorian armor of the era, decorated to the wearer's preference.<ref name="O66">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref>

[[File:BuirkalorClassAirspeeders-Corruption.png|thumb|right|300px|Two of the Mandalorian Guard's [[Buirk'alor-class airspeeder|''Buirk'alor''-class airspeeders]]]]
Members of the Mandalorian Guard were trained to use a variety of weapons. The most common was the stun baton, favored by those Guardsmen who operated among the New Mandalorians<ref name="TBHC" /> as it's non-lethal nature fit their role as maintainers of security.<ref name="GuardEncyclopedia" /> Many Guardsmen also carried large, handheld shields that could halt blasterfire,<ref name="Corruption" /> and [[Mandalorian manacles]] were a regular component of Mandalorian police equipment; forged from nearly impervious [[Beskar/Legends|''beskar'']] [[Iron/Legends|iron]], the manacles were used to bind a [[Prisoner/Legends|captive's]] [[Limb/Legends|limbs]].<ref name="I80:HotM" /> Though the pacifistic New Mandalorians asked restraint of the Guard,<ref name="TBHC" /> several members carried blasters, including [[WESTAR-35 blaster pistol/Legends|WESTAR-35 blaster pistols]], in order to meet the needs of the job. [[Flamethrower/Legends|Flamethrowers]],<ref name="Corruption" /> such as the [[BT X-42 flamethrower|BT X-42]],<ref name="NewBattlefronts" /> and other heavy weapons were also available to Guardsmen should the need for them arise.<ref name="TBHC" />

The Mandalorian Guard utilized<ref name="Corruption" /> a number of vessels built by [[MandalMotors/Legends|MandalMotors]],<ref name="TCWIV">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Incredible Vehicles]]''</ref> a Mandalorian company [[MandalMotors tower|headquartered]] in Mandalore's [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Keldabe/Legends|Keldabe]].<ref name="O66" /> Mandalore's police force used [[Buirk'alor-class airspeeder|''Buirk'alor''-class airspeeders]]<ref name="TCWIV" />—displaying the word "POLICE" in [[Mando'a/Legends|''Mando'a'']] [[Mandalorian (writing system)/Legends|lettering]] at the nose<ref name="Corruption" />—to patrol the [[Skylane/Legends|skylanes]] of New Mandalorian cities, capitalizing on the [[Speeder/Legends|speeders']] powerful engines to quickly respond to emergencies.<ref name="TCWIV" /> The Guard also made use<ref name="TBHC" /> of [[Balutar-class swoop/Legends|''Balutar''-class swoops]], fast and nimble [[Speeder bike/Legends|speeder bikes]] whose patrol models carried twin [[Blaster cannon/Legends|cannons]], and had access to [[Aka'jor-class shuttle/Legends|''Aka'jor''-class shuttles]]<ref name="TCWIV" /> for missions that required travel beyond the capability of an [[Airspeeder/Legends|airspeeder]], including transit between Mandalore and it's [[Orbit/Legends|orbiting]] [[Moon/Legends|moon]], [[Concordia/Legends|Concordia]].<ref name="TCW:DoM" />

==History==
{{Quote|&hellip;we must be mindful that the New Mandalorian government closely monitors the Mandalorian Guard, particularly its elite units.|Tor Vizsla|<ref name="TBHC" />}}
The Mandalorian Guard was established as a police and emergency services organization on the planet Mandalore. Over [[Time/Legends|time]], the Guard earned a reputation for attracting Mandalorians into its ranks who wished to aid and protect their people. Following the rise of the pacifist New Mandalorian faction in the aftermath of the [[Mandalorian Excision]], elements of the Mandalorian Guard chose to offer their loyalty and service to the peaceful sect.<ref name="TBHC" /> Despite the New Mandalorians' attempts to forgo violence, the Mandalorian police force remained an active part of their society in order to ensure the welfare of the public and to maintain security.<ref name="GuardEncyclopedia" />

[[File:MandalorianGuardsmen.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The Mandalorian Guard in action]]
In the aftermath of the [[Great Clan Wars/Legends|Great Clan Wars]], during which the [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]]<ref name="TBHC" />—a radical and violent Mandalorian splinter group<ref name="I80:HotM" />—tried and failed to bring about the destruction of the peaceful New Mandalorians, the pacifist faction's newest leader, [[Duchess/Legends|Duchess]] [[Satine Kryze/Legends|Satine Kryze]], used her influence to reorganize the Mandalorian Guard. Over the [[Standard year/Legends|years]], individual units of the Guard had become power bases for singular clans, and Kryze moved to break up these clan concentrations via engineered promotions and a reform of the chain of command that saw units of the Guard composed of members from multiple clans. However, tensions developed between the Guard and the New Mandalorian Duchess as veteran Guardsmen grew resentful of less-qualified members being promoted in place of their more deserving peers for no reason other than their clan ties. While recovering from their losses suffered over the course of the Great Clan Wars, Death Watch attempted to recruit several of these dissatisfied Guardsmen to their cause, though they remained cautious of the New Mandalorian government's efforts to monitor the Guard. The Mandalorian Patrol, the Guard's Planetary Security Force, was also known to have Death Watch sympathizers among its membership at this time, focusing their attention more on criminal activity<ref name="TBHC" /> than the Mandalorian radicals.<ref name="I80:HotM" />

[[File:FennShysa-Hasbro.png|thumb|right|175px|Mandalorian constable [[Fenn Shysa]]]]During this time, [[Youngling/Legends|childhood]] friends [[Fenn Shysa]] and [[Tobbi Dala]] grew up off the coast of Mandalore's largest continent, eventually joining the Mandalorian police force as constables of the local province. After finishing a day's work, the two Mandalorian lawmen would enjoy a few mugs of [[Mandallian Narcolethe/Legends|Mandallian Narcolethe]] together.<ref name="I80:HotM" />

When the former [[Alpha-class Advanced Recon Commando|Advanced Recon Commando]] known as [[Spar]] defected from the Republic's [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army]], he came to Mandalore following the death of the [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] army's [[Clone template/Legends|progenitor]], the Mandalorian [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]].<ref name="I80:HotM" /> With the support of Fenn Shysa, by now a minor clan [[Chief/Legends|chieftain]]<ref name="O66" /> and a respected Mandalorian constable, Spar became the new [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor'']]—"Mandalore the Resurrector"—and began recruiting Mandalorian [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] for a new group of [[Mandalorian Supercommando|supercommandos]] known as the [[Mandalorian Protectors (Spar)|Mandalorian Protectors]]. In pursuit of his goal, Spar turned to Shysa's comrades in the Mandalorian police force, drawing close to two hundred willing recruits from their ranks to form the backbone of the Protector army.<ref name="I80:HotM" /> The Mandalorian Protectors entered the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] on the side of the Confederacy, becoming a renowned shock force capable of doing in one day what the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Separatist droid army]] couldn't accomplish in a [[Standard month/Legends|month]], but their role in the war ultimately came to an end after succumbing to a devastating Republic [[Mission to Norval II|ambush]] on [[Norval II]].<ref name="GaW" />

In [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]],<ref name="TMPDate">{{FactFile2014|21|21 BBY 3-6|Intrigues in the Outer Rim}}</ref> amidst the galaxy-spanning Clone Wars, the New Mandalorian capital city of [[Sundari/Legends|Sundari]] came under the [[Attack on the Memorial Shrine/Legends|attack]] of a [[Terrorist/Legends|terrorist]] [[Death Watch bomber/Legends|bomber]] associated with the violent Death Watch. When the culprit chose to [[Death/Legends|take his own life]] following a chase through the city with [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], Duchess Satine Kryze elected to return the body of the deceased [[Gender/Legends|man]] to his family on Mandalore's moon, Concordia. A [[Squad/Legends|squad]] of Mandalorian [[Police officer/Legends|police officers]] accompanied Concordia's [[Governor/Legends|Governor]] [[Pre Vizsla/Legends|Pre Vizsla]] in greeting the Duchess' [[Shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] upon her arrival at the [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] [[Hangar/Legends|hangar]]. While on Concordia, Kryze discovered the Death Watch was being led by Governor Vizsla with the support of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], only escaping a nearly fatal [[Fight on Concordia/Legends|encounter]] with the Mandalorian radicals due to the [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|efforts]] of Obi-Wan Kenobi. Later, having returned to Mandalore, Kryze was escorted from the [[Sundari Royal Palace/Legends|Sundari Royal Palace]] to the [[Sundari shipping docks/Legends|city's docks]] by the Mandalorian Guard, where her personal [[Starship/Legends|starship]] the [[Coronet/Legends|''Coronet'']] was waiting to take her to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].<ref name="TMP" /> As the Duchess stood before the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Galactic Senate/Legends|senate]] to denounce the threat of Death Watch, insisting that they did not speak for the whole of Mandalore, a [[Unidentified New Mandalorian scout/Legends|Mandalorian Guardsman]] was sent to [[Scout/Legends|scout]] the [[Death Watch hideout|Death Watch's hideout]] on Concordia. There, he witnessed a massing of Death Watch [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] equipped with [[Kom'rk-class fighter/transport/Legends|''Kom'rk''-class fighters]] and [[Armored Assault Tank/Legends|AAT]] [[Tank/Legends|tanks]], and the scout reported his findings back to the New Mandalorian Prime Minister, [[Almec/Legends|Almec]]. The Death Watch [[Army/Legends|army]] was ultimately forced to stand down when the Confederacy withdrew its support for their campaign.<ref name="TCW:DoM" />

[[File:Stopinthenameofthelaw-Corruption.png|thumb|right|300px|A Mandalorian police captain, flanked by Duchess [[Satine Kryze/Legends|Satine Kryze]], [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], and the [[Mandalorian Royal Guard/Legends|Royal Guard]]]]
Later that year,<ref name="CorruptionDate">{{FactFile2014|48|21 BBY 13-14|Corruption on Mandalore}}</ref> with Republic trade routes to Mandalore closed, the New Mandalorian people were forced to invest heavily in [[Black market/Legends|black market]] dealings in order to attain supplies. Corruption and greed spread through both the New Mandalorian government and the Mandalorian Guard, and several Guardsmen working with the [[New Mandalorian customs department/Legends|New Mandalorian customs department]] allowed a group of [[Moogan/Legends|Moogan]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] to operate out of a [[Sundari dock warehouse/Legends|dock warehouse]], importing [[Ardees Beverage/Legends|shipments]] of [[Tea/Legends|tea]] they then diluted with [[Poison/Legends|toxic]] levels of [[Slabin/Legends|slabin]] to maximize [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|profits]]. A number of New Mandalorian children fell ill as a result of drinking the poisoned tea, leading to an investigation into the source of the illness by Duchess Kryze and the Mandalorian Royal Guard. Tracking the smugglers to their base, a group of Mandalorian police and Royal Guardsmen led by Kryze confronted the corrupt Guardsmen protecting the warehouse, engaging the rogue officers and the smugglers inside in a [[Skirmish at the Sundari docks/Legends|firefight]] that ended with several smugglers dead and the others taken into custody. During the shootout, two members of the Mandalorian police were wounded by blasterfire, including the [[Unidentified Mandalorian police captain (Sundari)|police captain]]. Kryze subsequently ordered the warehouse and its contents burned, and in spite of the Guard captain's concerns over the loss of valuable forensic evidence, the Mandalorian police obeyed the Duchess' orders and proceeded to burn down the warehouse with several flamethrowers retrieved from their airspeeders.<ref name="Corruption" />

The Mandalorian Guard were among those hit hardest by the forces of the [[Shadow Collective/Legends|Shadow Collective]] during their [[Takeover of Mandalore/Legends|attack]] on the New Mandalorian people. [[Pyke Syndicate/Legends|Pyke Syndicate]] thugs and [[Black Sun foot soldier/Legends|Black Sun foot soldiers]] landed at the Sundari docks and ambushed members of the Guard. The criminal contingent overpowered the police, violently subduing and [[Prison/Legends|imprisoning]] the New Mandalorians in shipping containers.<ref name="Shades of Reason" /> In [[Peace Park/Legends|Peace Park]], [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] soldiers and [[Pyke/Legends|Pyke]] gunmen opened [[Lightfight|fire]] on the crowd, killing police and civilians alike in an indiscriminatory manner.<ref name="ShadowConspiracy">''[[The Clone Wars: Darth Maul: Shadow Conspiracy]]''</ref> And at the [[Mandalore Banking Center/Legends|Mandalore Banking Center]],<ref name="SoRGuide">{{SW|url=explore/the-clone-wars/ep515|text="Shades of Reason" - ''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide|nolive=1}}</ref> the Pykes led a team to rob the facility,<ref name="ShadowConspiracy" /> using the [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|combat]] prowess of their [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] ally [[Savage Opress/Legends|Savage Opress]] to [[Lightsaber/Legends|carve]] through the defending members of the Guard and enter the [[Bank/Legends|bank]]. Within short order, the Shadow Collective's operatives had overwhelmed New Mandalorian Guard forces across Mandalore, shaking the people's faith in Duchess Kryze's ability to keep them safe. Relief from the criminal onslaught came only with the arrival of the Death Watch, who struck back at the gangsters holding the docks of Sundari, securing the area and freeing the Guardsmen the [[Gangster/Legends|gangsters]] had taken hostage, while other Death Watch troops subdued the Shadow Collectives forces throughout the city. Death Watch leader Pre Vizsla personally defeated the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] Savage Opress, turning him over to police custody. For their actions against the Shadow Collective, the Mandalorian Guard and the people of Sundari were vocal in their praise of Death Watch. With the people's backing, Vizsla deposed Duchess Kryze and installed himself as the New Mandalorians' leader.<ref name="SoR">{{TCW|Shades of Reason}}</ref>

As the Clone Wars drew to a close in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], the victorious Galactic Republic was [[Declaration of a New Order|transformed]] into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], and the new government set its sights on occupying Mandalore<ref name="ImpCom501st">''[[Imperial Commando: 501st]]''</ref> just as its predecessor had during the Clone Wars.<ref name="TCW:DoM" /> Though the Empire's initial relations with Mandalore were cordial,<ref name="ImpCom501st" /> the Imperial presence soon became a tyrannical occupation, enslaving<ref name="GaW" /> and [[Mining/Legends|strip-mining]] Mandalore.<ref name="Sacrifice">''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]''</ref> To resist the Imperial occupation, a new iteration of the Mandalorian Protectors rose under ''Mand'alor'' Fenn Shysa, who again called upon elements of the elite Mandalorian police to aid in his guerrilla war with the Empire. Though it took time, in the end the Protectors were able to overcome the Imperials' hold on Mandalore, [[Battle of the City of Bone|defeating]] the Empire's [[Imperial Military/Legends|forces]] in the [[City of Bone]], before driving them fully from Mandalorian space.<ref name="GaW" />

==Behind the scenes==
Mandalorian police were first mentioned in the ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' article [[The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors|''The History of the Mandalorians'']], written by [[Abel G. Peña]] and published in [[January]] of [[2005]] as part of the magazine's [[Star Wars Insider 80|eightieth issue]].<ref name="I80:HotM" /> Four years later, in [[2009]], the ''[[Galaxy at War]]'' sourcebook again mentioned units of Mandalorian police and their impact on the foundation of both iterations of the Mandalorian Protectors.<ref name="GaW" /> On [[January 29]], [[2010]], the Mandalorian Guard appeared in full with the debut of "[[The Mandalore Plot]]," the twelfth episode of the [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' television series']] [[The Clone Wars: Season Two|second season]].<ref name="TMP" /> The Guard would go on to reappear in several subsequent episodes of the series, including "[[Duchess of Mandalore]],"<ref name="TCW:DoM" /> "[[Corruption (episode)|Corruption]],"<ref name="Corruption" /> "[[The Academy]],"<ref name="The Academy" /> and "[[Shades of Reason]]."<ref name="SoR" />

The [[Encyclopedia (StarWars.com)|Encyclopedia]], hosted on [[StarWars.com]] from [[September 13]], [[2011]] to [[July 1]], [[2014]], provided an informational entry for the Mandalorian Guard. While other sources suggested that the Mandalorian Guard and the Mandalorian Royal Guard were distinct, separate units, the Encyclopedia entry referenced both organizations as though they were interchangeable, even linking the Mandalorian Guard entry to the [[Wookieepedia]] article for the Royal Guard instead of this one.<ref name="GuardEncyclopedia" /> The Guard's entry in the [[canon]]ical [[Databank (2014-)|Databank]], which replaced the Encyclopedia on StarWars.com, continues to refer to both groups in an interchangeable manner.<ref name="Databank">{{Databank|mandalorian-guard|Mandalorian Guard}}</ref> The [[2013]] release of ''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]'', a reference book co-[[Author/Legends|authored]] by [[Jason Fry]], [[Daniel Wallace]], and [[Ryder Windham]], outlined further information on the Mandalorian Guard, including new context that denotes the Royal Guard as an elite unit of the Mandalorian Guard.<ref name="TBHC" />
